source.title: [re:DEFINICIJA] Fran Petar Reizl: Ako uspiješ u Hrvatskoj, možeš uspjeti bilo gdje (ep. 3)

summary.title_hr: [re:DEFINICIJA] Fran Petar Reizl: Ako uspiješ u Hrvatskoj, možeš uspjeti bilo gdje (ep. 3)
summary.abstract_hr: U ovoj epizodi podcasta Redefinicija voditelj Kruno razgovara s Franom Petrom Reizlom, poduzetnikom, dizajnerom, glazbenikom, suprugom i ocem četvero djece. Reizl opisuje svoj poduzetnički put: od obiteljskog brenda Vrsna čokolada, pokrenutog uz pomoć europskih fondova, do vlastitog brenda Reizl Snacks, koji proizvodi voćne pločice s adaptogenima. Govori o usklađivanju obitelji i posla na temelju kršćanskih vrijednosti, o plaćanju poreza, muževnosti u poslovnom svijetu te o izazovima mladih poduzetnika u Hrvatskoj, poput visokog PDV-a i nedostatka kulture poticanja. Predstavlja i svoj glazbeni rad te istraživanje obiteljskog podrijetla, kojim je otkrio da su mu preci bili češki graničari u Slavoniji. Razgovor završava blic-pitanjima i porukom mladim muškarcima da se ne boje ostvariti svoje snove.
key_points: Reizl je s roditeljima pokrenuo obiteljski brend Vrsna čokolada uz pomoć europskih fondova. Nakon šest do sedam godina učenja o proizvodnji i poslovanju pokrenuo je vlastiti brend Reizl Snacks, koji danas proizvodi male voćne pločice s adaptogenima.
U njegovoj obitelji muž radi, a supruga je više s djecom. Ističe da je takav raspored stvar dogovora i obostrane žrtve te da treba tražiti zlatnu sredinu između posla i obitelji.
Plaćanje PDV-a smatra sastavnim dijelom računice i poštuje načelo 'caru carevo, Bogu Božje'. Priznaje i da mu je bila pogreška što je odmah osnovao d.o.o. u sustavu PDV-a.
Prenosi izreku povratnika iz inozemstva da je onaj tko prođe test na hrvatskom tržištu spreman za bilo koje tržište.

Kao glavne izazove mladih poduzetnika u Hrvatskoj navodi visok PDV, nedostatak kulture poticanja i ohrabrivanja te nedostatak dugoročnog fokusa. Smatra da Hrvatska uz bolje liderstvo može postati poput Švicarske.
Poduzetnicima preporučuje da svoje ideje često raspravljaju s ljudima kojima vjeruju te da rano ustaju i razmišljaju u tišini.
Istraživanjem obiteljskog podrijetla otkrio je da su mu preci bili češki graničari u Slavoniji. Zaključio je da su svi ljudi, kao djeca Boga Oca, braća i sestre.
key_points_en: Together with his parents, Reizl launched the family brand Vrsna čokolada with the help of European funds. After six to seven years of learning about production and business, he launched his own brand Reizl Snacks, which today produces small fruit bars with adaptogens.

In his family, the husband works, and the wife is more with the children. He emphasizes that such an arrangement is a matter of agreement and mutual sacrifice, and that one should seek a golden mean between work and family.

He considers paying VAT an integral part of the calculation and respects the principle 'to Caesar what is Caesar's, to God what is God's'. He also admits that it was a mistake for him to immediately establish a d.o.o. in the VAT system.
He conveys a saying of returnees from abroad that anyone who passes the test on the Croatian market is ready for any market.

As the main challenges of young entrepreneurs in Croatia, he cites high VAT, the lack of a culture of stimulation and encouragement, and a lack of long-term focus. He believes that Croatia, with better leadership, can become like Switzerland.
He recommends that entrepreneurs frequently discuss their ideas with people they trust and that they wake up early and reflect in silence.
Through research into his family origin, he discovered that his ancestors were Czech border guards in Slavonija. He concluded that all people, as children of God the Father, are brothers and sisters.
summary.title_en: [re:DEFINICIJA] Fran Petar Reizl: If You Succeed in Croatia, You Can Succeed Anywhere (ep. 3)
summary.abstract_en: In this episode of the Redefinicija podcast, host Kruno talks with Fran Petar Reizl, an entrepreneur, designer, musician, husband, and father of four children. Reizl describes his entrepreneurial journey: from the family brand Vrsna čokolada, launched with the help of European funds, to his own brand Reizl Snacks, which produces fruit bars with adaptogens. He speaks about balancing family and work based on Christian values, about paying taxes, masculinity in the business world, and about the challenges of young entrepreneurs in Croatia, such as high VAT and the lack of a culture of encouragement. He also presents his musical work and research into his family origins, through which he discovered that his ancestors were Czech border guards in Slavonija. The conversation ends with quick-fire questions and a message to young men not to be afraid to realize their dreams.
